teams.heading: Ireland 'A' squad to face Fiji, with Tadhg Furlong cleared to play
teams.body: Ireland's 'A' side are set to face Fiji, a fixture flagged alongside news that Tadhg Furlong is cleared to play. Furlong also avoided a ban after a 'unanimous' Disciplinary Committee decision over an alleged testicle grab. For Fiji, the Ireland match is a reminder that the Jake White era has a busy November, with Fiji having beaten Japan 34-28 last weekend and facing France, Ireland and Italy in the upcoming Tests.

lead.why: The Nathan Hughes squad story is already on the tab today, and the two league items are not union, so the Ireland 'A' fixture is the only remaining union candidate.

teams.heading: England A face Bernasconi-led Argentina XV in uncapped Bath clash
teams.body: England A host Argentina XV in an uncapped match in Bath on Friday, a fixture that gives fringe players from both sides a shot at test call-ups. Argentina head coach Álvaro Galindo, a former Puma, has named a 27-man squad headlined by hooker Bernardo Bernasconi of Benetton, with Harlequins prop Pedro Delgado and Bristol Bears flanker Benjamín Grondona also selected. Both sides play four capped tests in the November Internationals.

lead.why: The only fresh men's England item in the shortlist; the others are either women's rugby, Premiership coverage already covered, or background.

teams.heading: Argentina bring back Facundo Isa for Ireland test, replacing injured Santiago Grondona
teams.body: Argentina's first Nations Championship squad includes a returning veteran for the visit to Lansdowne Road: Facundo Isa, who missed international duty in 2024 and 2026 and only played for Argentina in July 2025, comes in for the injured Santiago Grondona. Felipe Contepomi's 33-man group has also lost Thomas Gallo, Santiago Carreras and Joaquín Oviedo to injury, and Franco Molina, a regular in recent selections, is absent.

teams.heading: Quesada calls November's four Tests one of Italy's most demanding challenges
teams.body: Gonzalo Quesada has framed Italy's November block as one of the most demanding challenges in the national team's history: four consecutive Tests against sides he says are all among the world's top ten, starting with South Africa in Turin, then Argentina in Genoa and Fiji in Udine before the final leg in London. He sees it as a test of the group's character, and says Italy must impose their own rugby rather than imitate others. Seventeen players are unavailable.

lead.why: It is the only Italy national-team item in the shortlist, and it adds the coach's framing of the four-Test window that earlier editions did not cover.

teams.heading: Finn Russell has no plans to end Scotland career after World Cup
teams.body: Finn Russell has confirmed he has no plans to end his Scotland career after the Rugby World Cup in Australia, the first time he has publicly confirmed it. The 34-year-old, who will be 35 by the time the tournament kicks off, has this year and next on his Bath contract and says: 'I'm keen to keep playing.' With New Zealand due at Murrayfield on Saturday, that is a useful signal.

lead.why: The freshest genuinely new Scotland international item, covering Russell's contract and future plans rather than the Pollock and All Blacks interview already run today.

teams.heading: WRU expresses interest in sending two Welsh clubs into English Premiership
teams.body: WalesOnline reports the WRU has expressed interest in two Welsh clubs joining the Gallagher Premiership, with talks under way with the RFU and Premiership Rugby. A move could come as early as next season, though the following campaign is seen as more realistic. The WRU still insists it is committed to four URC teams until 2027/28, but a letter to Swansea Council speaks of 'ongoing confidential developments'. With the Ospreys and Scarlets still battling to survive, the summit in December could revisit the four-club model.

lead.why: The WRU's interest in putting two Welsh clubs into the English Premiership affects all four professional sides, which makes it a bigger men's story than the other items on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Thomas Gallo and Santiago Carreras ruled out of Argentina squad with injuries
teams.body: Argentina's squad was hit before the London camp had even started. Thomas Gallo (Lyon) and Santiago Carreras (Bath) were lost to injuries on the eve of the three-day London camp in late October, with Mateo Soler (Dogos) and Rodrigo Martínez (Dragons) called up in their places. Centre Santiago Chocobares was awaiting the outcome of a head injury assessment, with Matías Moroni on stand-by. Later coverage lists Gallo and Carreras among players out with long-term injuries.

lead.why: The Gallo and Carreras injuries and the Chocobares head-injury check are the squad story the edition has not yet covered, and the Isa and Bernasconi stories are already on the tab.

teams.heading: Roar column said Wallabies 'well and truly stuck' in second tier
teams.body: A January column from The Roar asked whether Australia is ready for the biggest World Cup ever, arguing the Wallabies are 'well and truly stuck in second tier of teams'. It also questioned whether a 24-team tournament risks diluting quality. The question still hangs over next year's home World Cup, and Australia still need an answer at No. 10: coach Les Kiss, who has just recalled Kurtley Beale, says he will reassess the position after the next Super Rugby Pacific season.

teams.heading: Japan's new kick-catch tactic is now being countered, analysis argues
teams.body: Japan have used a new kick-catch method since the start of this year, with player B rather than player A taking the high ball, an analysis published on Thursday argues. The writer says it significantly reduces the risk of penalties for escorting, where penalties have become stricter. The downside is that the catcher must run backwards with support only from player A, and opponents are already countering it. The writer says the kick-catching issue was also highlighted in the Fiji match.

lead.why: It is the only men's Japan item in the pack that is new today, and it covers how Japan's tactics are being read after the Fiji match.

teams.heading: Saula Ma'u picked after Tyrel Lomax ruled out with neck issue
teams.body: Tyrel Lomax has been ruled out of the All Blacks' squad with a neck issue, and Saula Ma'u has been picked after Lomax was ruled out. The Highlander joins Pasilio Tosi as one of the two big tightheads in the 36-man Nations Championship group, and has yet to earn a cap. He is expected to make his Test debut next month, and will look to put himself in the frame for the Rugby World Cup next year.

lead.why: Fresh squad news from the same pack: Lomax's neck issue has opened a spot for Ma'u, a different angle from the size debate already reported.

teams.heading: Kolbe, Etzebeth, Esterhuizen and Pollard miss touring squad through injury, Hansen says
teams.body: Cheslin Kolbe, Eben Etzebeth, Andre Esterhuizen and Handré Pollard have all been left out of Rassie Erasmus' touring squad through injury, but Sir Steve Hansen believes the head coach is deliberately managing the group. Speaking on the Rugby Unity podcast, Hansen said Erasmus is giving Etzebeth a breather ahead of the World Cup. Erasmus has included six uncapped players to cover the setbacks, and Hansen believes this will be the final window for experiments before the tournament.
